scope: Bounded review of new Cantia/Kent name correspondence, overview and boundary warning, and added Old English writing passage only. Twelve inherited body passages were not independently re-certified. No browser sessions or runtime edits.

sourcesChecked.scope: Direct article, printed page 317, Cantuarii section explicitly identifies Bede's Cantia as Kent. Broader speculative etymologies were not relied on.

Direct editorial transcription folio 2r and corresponding literal translation. Exact quoted Old English sentence, including L and thorn/eth spelling and punctuation, matches. Fifty sceattas for hair-seizing is supported. Checked scholarly transcription, not manuscript image.

geometry.method: Independently decoded first Cantia and Kent TopoJSON features with topojson-client.
geometry.assessment: Cantia grossly extends beyond historical Kent. Public overview and alias summary explicitly reject its outline as a verified border and identify coverage dates as map intervals, not two kingdoms. Appropriate.

writingAssessment: Exact attested Old English from Monk's edition with attributed translation, no currency conversion. Public copy explicitly distinguishes twelfth-century witness from much earlier law code; inherited manuscript-date paragraph retained.

budgetCheck.method: Overview, period titles/summaries, all body passages, ending, Kent summary and Cantia alias summary; Unicode word tokens.
